plan.tagline: Read, imagine, and give every child a story to take home.
plan.concept: Host a family-friendly afternoon for 120 guests at Swedish American Museum, combining picture-book readings, a children’s craft station, and a small live music set. Guests can donate at the welcome table and receive a book to read with a child at home.
plan.format: Saturday afternoon family social with readings, activities, and live music, approximately 3 hours
plan.date_window: A Saturday in May, ideally 2:00 PM–5:00 PM
plan.taste_summary: Supporters enjoy picture books and a strong interest in Where the Wild Things Are, suggesting a playful, story-centered celebration. The program should feel warm, imaginative, and easy for families to join.

run_of_show.title: Welcome and story launch
run_of_show.detail: Check in, receive a reading passport, and hear the event goal and program overview.

run_of_show.title: Picture-book reading hour
run_of_show.detail: Facilitators share picture books, including a featured reading inspired by Where the Wild Things Are.

run_of_show.title: Family reading workshop
run_of_show.detail: Guests create simple story prompts and practice reading together with their children.

run_of_show.title: Children’s craft and book table
run_of_show.detail: Kids make bookmarks and character masks while families browse donated books.

run_of_show.title: Live music set
run_of_show.detail: The Mad Gear and Missile Kid performs a short set for children and adults.

run_of_show.title: Give a book, share a story
run_of_show.detail: Guests make a donation, choose a book, and take home a simple family reading activity.

promotion_angles.angle: Create short podcast-style clips about why early reading matters, featuring brief read-alouds and guest reflections.
Share a documentary-style profile of a family using the nonprofit’s free reading programs and invite guests to join the celebration.
Use playful, kid-friendly promotional clips featuring picture-book characters, simple jokes, and reading challenges.
Invite local creators to share a lively “family night out” invitation while keeping the campaign welcoming for families.
Tell short, dramatic story-based updates about children discovering books and reading together at home.

sponsor_pitch.subject: Bring a story to life: support Wild Pages Story Day
sponsor_pitch.opening: Your organization can help 120 families celebrate children’s literacy at Swedish American Museum in May. The afternoon combines picture-book readings, creative activities, live music, and book donations for kids.
sponsor_pitch.audience: Supporters show a clear preference for picture books and an interest in Where the Wild Things Are. Your audience and event visitors can connect through a welcoming, family-centered experience centered on stories, learning, and community.
benefits: Receive visible recognition at the event
Connect your brand with children’s literacy
sponsor_pitch.ask: Please consider supporting the event with a small cash contribution, in-kind books, refreshments, or a book giveaway. Together, we can make sure more children leave with a story of their own.

baseline.concept: Host an affordable, family-friendly reading festival inspired by Where the Wild Things Are, with book giveaways and free literacy activities. Turn donated space, books, and volunteer support into a memorable May fundraising event.
